response.message: We're building an Azure incident explainer: OpenTelemetry logs and traces flow through Event Hubs, a redaction Function and Azure Data Explorer, then into a Container Apps analysis runtime that calls Azure OpenAI and returns an answer citing exact trace and log IDs to a signed-in operator. None of these Azure services has a native generator here yet, so every block still needs engineering work. Nothing is deployed, and no region or account access has been checked. For the first local test, we replay a synthetic incident fixture through the redactor and a scripted mock model; the fixture includes planted secrets, an injected instruction in a log, a missing span and a duplicate batch. That proves the plumbing and safeguards work, but not the quality of the reasoning, which needs a separate evaluation against a real Azure OpenAI deployment. Which country must this log and trace data stay in?

proposal.title: Azure log/trace incident explainer – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: collect synthetic OpenTelemetry logs and traces, redact secrets, store them with idempotent keys, retrieve the evidence and analyse it with Azure OpenAI, then return a cited answer to an Entra-authenticated operator. Assumptions: the data is synthetic, the region is still to be selected, and no account or model access has been verified. All Azure blocks are design-only: there are no native generators yet, so engineering is required. Log text is treated as untrusted data and is never used as instructions.

data.label: Synthetic services (OTel)
data.description: Existing synthetic services that emit OpenTelemetry logs and spans with trace, span and log IDs. They sit outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Telemetry collection
data.description: Takes in OTLP-exported log and trace batches. Partitioned by trace ID to keep ordering within each trace.

data.label: Redaction & normalisation
data.description: Event Hubs trigger. Masks secrets and tokens before storage or model input, normalises timestamps and writes records with deterministic keys (trace, span, log ID) so a replay is idempotent and the timeline stays consistent.

data.label: Telemetry store & search
data.description: Holds the redacted logs and spans. Answers KQL queries for the incident timeline, trace trees and gap detection (missing spans). Ingestion deduplicates on record keys.

data.label: AI analysis runtime
data.description: Gets the evidence through a fixed, allowlisted KQL query tool and passes log text to the model as quoted data only, so model output cannot trigger tool calls. Checks that every conclusion cites existing trace or log IDs, and reports uncertainty when spans are missing. Returns the cited answer to the operator.

data.label: Incident reasoning model
data.description: Chat model deployment that receives only redacted evidence. The model, quota and regional availability are not yet verified.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Engineer who asks why the incident happened and reviews the cited answer.

data.label: Operator sign-in
data.description: Authenticates operators and issues the tokens that the runtime validates.

data.label: Runtime observability
data.description: Audit of questions, evidence IDs used, refusals, guard failures and latency. This is separate from the analysed synthetic telemetry.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If secrets leak into the prompt or the store, credentials are exposed.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Redact secrets before model input.
requirementDrafts.statement: Secrets and credentials are redacted before any log or span text is stored for analysis or sent to the model.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Operators must be able to verify each claim, and uncited claims are untrustworthy.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Link conclusions to exact trace or log IDs.
requirementDrafts.statement: Every conclusion references exact trace, span or log IDs that exist in the store.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without this, an attacker who can write a log line could steer the system.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Prompt injection in a log cannot issue tool calls.
requirementDrafts.statement: Log content is treated as untrusted data; instructions embedded in logs cannot trigger tool calls or queries outside the allowlist.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Invented root causes mislead incident response.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Missing spans yield uncertainty rather than invented causes.
requirementDrafts.statement: When spans are missing, the answer states the uncertainty instead of asserting a cause.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Duplicates or reordering would corrupt the causal analysis.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Repeated ingestion preserves a consistent incident timeline.
requirementDrafts.statement: Re-ingesting the same telemetry produces an identical incident timeline, with no duplicates or reordering.

response.message: No runtime checks have run yet (0 checks, status blocked), so this design hasn't been validated. The empty failures list doesn't mean anything passed. The first blocker is the Event Hubs telemetry collection. None of the typed generator contracts covers Event Hubs, Functions, Data Explorer, Container Apps, Azure OpenAI or Entra. The only Azure contract is private object storage, and switching to it would shrink our incident explainer down to storage, so I'm not proposing any graph change. Each of these components needs a native Azure implementation in the product before local emulation can test anything. The first useful reproducer is your synthetic incident fixture: planted secrets, an injected instruction, a missing span and a duplicate batch. Even after those checks pass, the mocked model only shows that the safeguards and plumbing work. It won't tell us whether the reasoning is any good. That needs a separate evaluation against a real Azure OpenAI deployment, and we haven't confirmed one exists. Before we pick a region and size the implementation work, one thing would help most: which country must this log and trace data stay in?
